values.label: health policy and administrative management
values.definition: Health sector policy, planning, and programmes; aid to health ministries and public health administration; institution capacity building and advice; medical insurance programmes; health system strengthening and health governance; and unspecified health activities.

blocks.title: Gates Foundation disbursements to reproductive health, 2009 to 2024
G7 bilateral ODA disbursements to reproductive health by provider, 2009 to 2024

frames.text:
From 2009 to 2024, funding to population policy, programmes, and reproductive health (OECD CRS sector 130) from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation grew substantially, positioning it above nearly all individual G7 countries except the United States. Data from the OECD Creditor Reporting System (CRS) shows the following trends in current US dollars.

Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
- 2009: $398 million
- 2024: $774 million

G7 bilateral ODA disbursements (by member)
- United States: $5.09 billion in 2009 to $9.07 billion in 2024
- United Kingdom: $474 million in 2009 to $319 million in 2024
- Canada: $69.7 million in 2009 to $319 million in 2024
- Germany: $193 million in 2009 to $110 million in 2024
- France: $28.0 million in 2009 to $70.5 million in 2024
- Japan: $55.4 million in 2009 to $33.3 million in 2024
- Italy: $12.7 million in 2009 to $7.11 million in 2024

Summary: While the United States remains by far the largest provider of reproductive health assistance, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation's disbursements reached $774 million by 2024, surpassing the bilateral contributions of every other G7 country individually (the next highest being the UK and Canada at approximately $319 million each).
